les: Hoe jy iemand se lewensverhaal uitvind
kaps_punt: Klastyd vir projekwerk; Geskiedenis navorsingsprojek vir Graad 6: 'n Biografie van 'n Suid-Afrikaner wat bygedra het tot die vestiging van demokrasie

items.bewering: Die mens oor wie jy skryf, is 'n Suid-Afrikaner wat ons demokrasie help bou het.
items.bron: CAPS Social Sciences Gr 4-6 (DBE), Grade 6 History Term 3, printed p. 44: 'History research project for Grade 6: A biography of a South African who has contributed to building democracy.' https://www.education.gov.za/Portals/0/CD/National%20Curriculum%20Statements%20and%20Vocational/CAPS%20IP%20%20SOCIAL%20SCIENCES%20%20WEB.pdf. Note, not a factual error: CAPS sets no gender, while the lesson refers to the subject as 'sy/haar' throughout; a learner could read that the person must be a woman.

items.bewering: 'n Biografie vertel een werklike mens se lewensverhaal. ... Skryf jou biografie in tydsorde van haar vroeë jare af. Leef sy nog, loop dit tot vandag toe. Sê ook waarom daardie lewe saak maak.
items.bron: Dictionary.com 'biography' (an account of a real person's life written by someone else, covering its main events) https://www.dictionary.com/browse/biography; CAPS Gr 4-6 SS s. 2.4.3 skills table ('chronological order'; heritage: 'how and why people and events are publicly remembered'), printed p. 11.

items.bewering: Moenie dadelik begin soek nie, maar skryf eers neer wat jy oor hierdie mens wil uitvind. Soek dan 'n antwoord op elke vraag. Sonder vrae lees jy sommer alles wat jy kan kry.
items.bron: CAPS Gr 4-6 SS s. 2.1 (learners must be encouraged to ask Who? What? When? Why?), s. 2.4.1 ('History is a process of enquiry and involves asking questions about the past'), s. 2.4.3 ('Selecting relevant information ... Some information that is found will not be relevant to the question'), printed pp. 8, 10-11.

items.bewering: Wanneer sy gebore is en of sy nog leef. / Wat sy gedoen het. / Waarom mense haar werk vandag onthou.
items.bron: Suggested questions, not factual claims; they match CAPS s. 2.4.1 ('What happened? When did it happen?') and the s. 2.4.3 heritage skill ('how and why people ... are publicly remembered'), printed pp. 10-11.

items.bewering: Jy vind jou antwoorde in bronne, en jy het meer as een bron nodig.
items.bron: CAPS Gr 4-6 SS s. 2.4.3 ('using more than one kind of written information'; 'checking to see if the information is accurate - comparing ... with other information'), printed p. 11; SAHO History Skills Pack, Source Analysis p. 1 (corroboration) https://sahistory.org.za/sites/default/files/archive_files/Clrm_Tech_Skills_Source_Analysis.pdf

items.bewering: 'n Primêre bron kom van iemand wat self daar was, soos 'n brief, 'n foto of 'n onderhoud met haar. 'n Sekondêre bron kom van iemand wat nie daar was nie, soos 'n geskiedenisboek of 'n dokumentêr.
items.bron: The examples are correct: letters, photographs and interviews are primary, and history books and documentaries are secondary (library guides, e.g. https://libguides.hccfl.edu/libraryjargon/primarysecondary; SAHO History Skills Pack p. 2). What is in doubt is the test the sentence teaches, which is only whether the maker was there. Sources disagree on the test. SAHO's CAPS-based skills pack defines primary as 'a source directly from the event it refers to' and secondary as 'written/created after an event', and lists newspaper articles and cartoons as primary. historyskills.com says 'the main difference ... is when they were made', with later eyewitness memoirs as an exception (https://historyskills.com/source-criticism/analysis/source-kind-and-type). The Stellenbosch Geskiedenis Opstelgids, quoted in search results, says primary sources 'word geskep in die tyd waarin die gebeurtenis ... plaasvind'. Library guides list government records such as births and census returns as primary. Under the lesson's 'was daar / was nie daar nie' rule, a newspaper report or cartoon from the time by someone who was not present, or an official record such as a birth certificate, comes out secondary. These are exactly what a learner meets when finding out 'wanneer sy gebore is'. Sources agree with the lesson that a later eyewitness account is primary. A person must decide the wording; it is likely a shared definition across the subject.

items.bewering: Albei soorte is nuttig, en hulle vertel nie altyd dieselfde nie.
items.bron: CAPS Gr 4-6 SS s. 2.4.3 ('Explaining why events in the past are often interpreted differently'; 'Seeing something ... from more than one point of view') and s. 2.4.4 (multi-perspective approach), printed pp. 11-12; Stellenbosch guide via search excerpt ('secondary sources provide background and help to confirm facts').

items.bewering: Twee bronne verskil soms, en daarom toets jy elke belangrike feit teen 'n tweede bron.
items.bron: CAPS Gr 4-6 SS s. 2.4.3 ('Deciding about whether information can be trusted ... checking to see if the information is accurate - comparing where the information came from with other information'), printed p. 11; SAHO History Skills Pack p. 1 ('Does the source's information corroborate with other historical sources?').

items.bewering: Een bron kan sê sy is op 'n plaas gebore, en 'n ander sê in 'n dorp.
items.bron: A hypothetical example about no real person, so there is no fact to verify. It is a plausible case of sources disagreeing as CAPS s. 2.4.3 describes (printed p. 11).

items.bewering: Moenie die weergawe kies wat die beste klink nie. Skryf eerder dat die bronne verskil of laat die punt uit.
items.bron: 'die beste' is in an instruction, not a factual superlative. The advice agrees with SAHO History Skills Pack p. 1 ('If a source contradicts another source use the two different sources to give a balanced view') and CAPS s. 2.4.3 (debating 'on the basis of the available evidence').

items.bewering: Hierdie stap onderskei navorsing van raaiwerk.
items.bron: Dictionary.com / Collins 'research': 'systematic investigation to establish facts', https://www.dictionary.com/browse/research; CAPS s. 2.4.3 treats checking information against other sources as part of a 'rigorous process of enquiry' (printed pp. 10-11).

items.bewering: Skryf die gebeure in tydsorde neer en nie in die volgorde waarin jy hulle gevind het nie.
items.bron: CAPS Gr 4-6 SS s. 2.4.3 ('sets out the relevant information in a logical way and in chronological order') and s. 2.4.4 'Time and chronology', printed pp. 11-12.

items.bewering: 'n Ry datums is nog nie 'n verhaal nie, want die verhaal lê tussen die datums.
items.bron: The figure maps soundly: the 'story between the dates' is the causes and links between events. That matches CAPS s. 2.4.4 'Cause and effect' and the s. 2.4.3 requirement of 'a logical line of argument' (printed pp. 11-12). It does not suggest that dates are unimportant, because the same block requires chronological order. A learner reasoning further from it is not led astray.

items.bewering: Skryf elke deel in jou eie woorde, want afskryf is nie navorsing nie. Sê ook in een sin waar jy jou inligting gekry het.
items.bron: School library guide 'Plagiarism is not just stealing, it's lousy research' (https://sites.google.com/chelseaschools.com/chelsea-hs-library/avoiding-plagiarism); Victoria University of Wellington on plagiarism as copying without referencing the original author (https://www.wgtn.ac.nz/students/study/exams/academic-integrity/plagiarism).

items.bewering: 'n Verhaal oor 'n werklike mens se lewe, geskryf deur iemand anders as daardie mens.
items.bron: Dictionary.com 'biography': written account of a person's life by someone else, as distinct from an autobiography, https://www.dictionary.com/browse/biography

items.bewering: 'n Manier van regeer waar die mense self kies wie regeer.
items.bron: Britannica Dictionary 'democracy' (government in which people choose leaders by voting) https://www.britannica.com/dictionary/democracy; Britannica summary (power exercised by the people directly or through elected representatives) https://www.britannica.com/summary/democracy. This is a simplification but not a false one, and it fits the South African case (CAPS p. 44: democracy since 1994, voting in national elections).

items.bewering: 'n Bron is iets waaruit ons kan leer - 'n foto, 'n geskrif, 'n storie, 'n onderhoud of 'n voorwerp - oor nou of oor lank gelede.
items.bron: CAPS Gr 4-6 SS s. 2.4.3 (information from 'text, visual material ..., songs, poems and interviews with people') and s. 2.4.4 (history is interpretation of 'information from various sources'), printed pp. 11-12; library guides list artefacts and objects as sources (https://libguides.hccfl.edu/libraryjargon/primarysecondary).

items.bewering: 'n Bron wat van iemand kom wat self daar was: die mens self, of iemand wat dit gesien het.
items.bron: This is the same doubt as the 'Twee soorte bronne' item. An eyewitness or participant source is primary in every definition found. The definition is not complete, though, because SAHO's CAPS-based skills pack (p. 2: 'a source directly from the event it refers to'; newspaper articles and cartoons as primary), historyskills.com ('made during the historical period that is being investigated') and library guides (birth and census records) also count material made at the time by people who were not witnesses. Under this wording a birth certificate or a newspaper report from the time is not primary. Sources disagree on which test leads, so a person must decide the wording, which is probably a shared definition.

items.bewering: Dit bly 'n primêre bron, ook as sy dit jare later vertel.
items.bron: Library guides treat memoirs and oral histories recorded long after the event as primary (University of Illinois primary source module https://www.library.illinois.edu/village/primarysource/mod1/pg11.htm; Georgetown oral history guide https://guides.library.georgetown.edu/c.php?g=1309863). historyskills.com gives a soldier's 1965 memoir of the First World War as primary 'since they were personally there'. SAHO's short definition does not address this case.

items.bewering: 'n Bron waarin iemand wat nie self daar was nie, vertel of verklaar wat gebeur het deur op ander bronne te steun, soos 'n geskiedenisboek of 'n dokumentêr.
items.bron: CASRAI 'secondary source' (examines or explains earlier material, author usually not an eyewitness) https://casrai.org/learn/secondary-source; library guides list history books and documentaries that analyse primary sources as secondary (https://libguides.hccfl.edu/libraryjargon/primarysecondary); Stellenbosch guide via search excerpt ('Sekondêre bronne sintetiseer en interpreteer primêre inligting').

items.bewering: Dit hang nie af van wanneer dit gemaak is nie.
items.bron: No source found says that when a source was made is irrelevant, and the main sources make it central. SAHO History Skills Pack p. 2, which is CAPS-based, defines secondary as 'A source that is written/created after an event. Usually based on primary sources.' (https://sahistory.org.za/sites/default/files/archive_files/Clrm_Tech_Skills_Source_Analysis.pdf). historyskills.com: 'The main difference between a primary and a secondary source is when they were made.' The Stellenbosch Geskiedenis Opstelgids (search excerpt): 'Primêre bronne word geskep in die tyd waarin die gebeurtenis ... plaasvind.' What is true is narrower: a later account by an eyewitness stays primary, which the primary-source entry already says.
items.regstelling: Remove the categorical sentence. If something must stand there, write the true, narrower form: a secondary source is usually made later, by someone who relies on other sources. When it was made does count, because something made at the time, such as a newspaper report or an official record, is usually counted as primary. This is probably a shared subject definition, so it goes to a person before a writer changes it.

items.bewering: Die volgorde waarin dinge gebeur het, van die eerste tot die laaste.
items.bron: 'eerste' and 'laaste' here mean order, not a historical first. The definition matches CAPS s. 2.4.4 'Time and chronology' ('place events in the order in which they happened in time'), printed p. 12.

items.bewering: Die manier waarop een bron iets vertel.
items.bron: Wiktionary 'weergawe' (Afrikaans; rendering, portrayal) https://wiki.neonvagabond.xyz/content/wiktionary_en_all_nopic_2024-05/A/weergawe; English-Afrikaans 'version' = 'weergawe' https://jmarian.com/af/en-version. These are thin, community-edited sources, but they are consistent with the sense used. No authoritative Afrikaans dictionary page was reached.

items.bewering: Om self uit te vind wat waar is en dit na te gaan.
items.bron: Dictionary.com / Collins 'research': 'systematic investigation to establish facts or principles', https://www.dictionary.com/browse/research; Vocabulary.com 'research' https://www.vocabulary.com/dictionary/research

opsomming: The lesson says a secondary source 'does not depend on when it was made', and that is contradicted: South African History Online's CAPS-based definition and other history sources make when a source was made central. Its 'was the maker there?' test for primary and secondary sources is disputed, because under that test a newspaper report or birth certificate from the time would count as secondary, so a person must decide what the probably shared definitions should say; everything else checks out.
